answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive at the inlet: each new key must post a signed epoch answer that peers attest, and any sibling funded from the same path inherits its first failure. The ledge holding that scheme up is the small repeated cost of being right - cheap to pay once, ruinous to pay a thousand times. A sybil's real delta is the gap between identities it can mint and the reputation it can actually afford.
